bluf: Reuters, The Guardian and France 24 reported cyberattacks targeting emergency alert apps in Ukraine and Russia, with false nuclear alerts reported in Ukraine. France 24 reported Iran offered a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear talks with the United States, while Israel’s prime minister said he wanted to “finish the job” first.

changes.text: Updated since previous brief: Ukraine and Russia report fake emergency alerts after cyberattacks target apps

items.text: Ukraine’s and Russia’s emergency alert apps were targeted by cyberattacks, and false nuclear alerts were reported in Ukraine; The Guardian also reported false chemical-attack and street-to-street fighting warnings in Kyiv. The incident time was not stated.
France 24 reported that Iran said it had a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear talks with the United States; Netanyahu said he wanted to “finish the job” first.
BBC News World reported fighting had returned to the Kherson region after a six-day truce.
BBC News World reported that dozens of supermarkets in seven European countries dumped large quantities of food after refrigerators and freezers were targeted in a cyberattack.
Reuters reported that North Korea said a US-South Korea nuclear drill showed the need for a stronger nuclear deterrent.
Reuters reported that Trump floated a concept for a US-Canada deal including a pipeline while talking to Carney.
